clue.text: No order for tea — too fat

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, a size for someone too fat for standard sizes

explanation.surface: A complaint that a cup of tea has been refused because the drinker is overweight.
explanation.definitionFit: Total confusion is the absence of any order or arrangement.

clue.text: Young Alfred, in the grip of illness, needs a source of energy

indicators.note: being held in the grip of something puts the name inside the illness

parts.note: a cold is a common illness
Alfie is a pet form of Alfred, as for a young boy

explanation.surface: A boy named Alfred, laid low by sickness, needs something to give him energy.
explanation.definitionFit: A region with coal deposits supplies fuel, a source of power.

clue.text: Irish missionary, top judo expert?

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the figure 1 standing as the letter I
a dan is a grade of black belt in judo, and a holder of it

explanation.surface: Describing an Irish preacher as also a first-class martial artist.
explanation.walkthrough: Saint Aidan was an Irish monk who founded the monastery at Lindisfarne in the 7th century.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Aidan of Lindisfarne was an Irish monk who evangelised Northumbria.

clue.text: Normal Sicilian beginnings in track record of Godfather

indicators.note: the initials are placed inside the word for an animal's trail

parts.note: spoor is the track or trail left by an animal

indicators.note: beginnings asks for the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Sicilian Mafia normality shown in the Godfather's track record.
explanation.definitionFit: A godparent at a christening takes on responsibility for the child, being a backer or guarantor.

clue.text: Unprepared for a piece of music

explanation.surface: A musician admits to being unready for a particular piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An unrehearsed speech is ad-libbed, and the same word names a short free-form instrumental composition, as by Schubert or Chopin.

clue.text: Soviet police chief's identification with part of the West

parts.note: I is how a person identifies himself, as in 'I, Beria'
Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police

explanation.surface: A Soviet security boss is linked with a region of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iberian peninsula of Spain and Portugal forms the south-western corner of Europe.

clue.text: A guest of Her Majesty's?

parts.note: a guest of Her Majesty is slang for a prisoner, but Her Majesty's is also a London theatre

explanation.surface: Euphemism for someone serving time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guest of Her Majesty' is a jokey British term for a prisoner; Her Majesty's is a West End theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone attending a show at a theatre is one of its audience.

clue.text: Topical change of view

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of letters in the preceding word

explanation.surface: A shift in viewpoint on a current issue.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to sight or vision, so concerning what is viewed.

clue.text: "Peter and the Dwarf' about to provide the entertainment

indicators.note: the two names are placed around the little word

parts.note: Peter Pan, J. M. Barrie's boy who never grew up
Mime is the Nibelung dwarf in Wagner's Ring cycle

explanation.surface: A show called Peter and the Dwarf is about to be staged as entertainment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About to' looks like 'soon going to'; 'about' puts PAN and MIME around TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is the traditional British Christmas stage show, a comic family entertainment, Peter Pan being a favourite.

clue.text: The: peace people started to smoke in conjunction

annotationWithheld.why: The peace people started to smoke in conjunction (5), as printed: UN for 'peace people' and LIT for 'started to smoke' give UN+LIT, not UNTIL, and 'The' has no job; no sound parse found
annotationWithheld.clue: The: peace people started to smoke in conjunction

clue.text: Dead Roman,.. perhaps, or mythical Greek

indicators.note: perhaps hints that the letters of the two preceding words could be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: Asking whether some deceased figure was a Roman or a Greek from legend.
explanation.definitionFit: In legend she was the Ethiopian princess chained to a rock and rescued by Perseus.

clue.text: Can you simultaneously believe its opposite?

definitions.text: Can you simultaneously believe its opposite?

parts.words: Can you simultaneously believe its opposite?
parts.note: a principle someone believes, and this word spelt backwards is the same word, so its reverse can be held at the same time

explanation.surface: A philosophical teaser about holding a belief and its contrary at once.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'opposite' is the word written backwards: a palindrome, so believing it and its reverse are one act.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctrine or principle that a person holds is something they believe.

clue.text: Where socially-inclined girls may be eating up some fish

parts.note: finishing your food means eating it up
a school is a group of fish swimming together

explanation.surface: Girls with a social bent might be found polishing off a plate of fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Such schools prepared well-off young women for society life, chiefly in the mid-20th century.
explanation.definitionFit: A private establishment that taught upper-class young women social graces before their debut.

clue.text: Member of the Dail's vast business interests?

indicators.note: a member of the parliament is read as the member sitting within the country's name

parts.note: the Dáil is the parliament of Eire, the Irish Republic
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Wondering about the large commercial holdings of an Irish parliamentarian.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprawling conglomerate controlled by one tycoon is often called a business realm or domain.

clue.text: It makes an obvious difference for a litigant

parts.note: plain means clear or obvious
a tiff is a minor quarrel, a difference of opinion

explanation.surface: Something that makes a clear difference to someone in a lawsuit.
explanation.definitionFit: The party who brings a case against another in court is a litigant.

clue.text: Acton girl becoming Australian singer

parts.note: Acton Bell was the pen name of Anne Brontë
bird is British slang for a girl

explanation.surface: A young woman from Acton, the London suburb, turns into a singer from Down Under.
explanation.walkthrough: Acton looks like the London district; it is Anne Brontë's pseudonym, Acton Bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bellbird is an Australasian songbird with a chiming call, so a feathered singer.

clue.text: Land of France is in depression — that'll keep people away

indicators.note: the French word sits inside the word for a hollow

parts.note: a dent is a small hollow or depression
terre is French for land

explanation.surface: French territory lying in a hollow may discourage visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that discourages people, such as a threat, stops them coming close.

clue.text: Strong chap guarded old railway director

indicators.note: the strongman holds the railway initials inside, as if protecting them

parts.note: a he-man is a muscular, macho man
the LMS was the London, Midland and Scottish Railway, a pre-1948 British line

explanation.surface: A burly man protected a former railway company's boss.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who steers a ship directs its course.

clue.text: The last place you would expect to find someone

definitions.text: The last place you would expect to find someone

parts.words: The last place you would expect to find someone
parts.note: read literally, the final spot where anyone is found is where they lie at the end of life

explanation.surface: An idiom for somewhere very unlikely to locate a person.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom means 'most unlikely place'; read literally it is where a person spends their final hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The bed on which someone dies is the final place they are found alive.

clue.text: Receptacle lost at sea? Lady's holding it

indicators.note: the pronoun for a lady holds the rearranged letters inside

parts.note: her is the pronoun for a lady

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters of lost are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman keeps hold of a container lost overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A leather case that holds a pistol on the hip is a kind of container.

clue.text: Possibly a grave sign of stress

explanation.surface: A solemn hint that someone is under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grave' is not solemn here: it is the grave mark over a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave mark is one kind of diacritic, and the same word names the emphasis on a syllable, marked in dictionaries.

clue.text: Framework was 1 ac to O'Casey

explanation.surface: Describing a structure as what an Irish playwright called disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 ac is CHAOS; in Sean O'Casey's Juno and the Paycock, Captain Boyle says the whole world is 'in a terrible state o' chassis'.
explanation.definitionFit: The base frame of a car is its load-bearing structure, and O'Casey's Dublin character mispronounces disorder this way.

clue.text: Person of no distinction, among many on earth

indicators.note: among says the letters lie inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An ordinary person, just one among many on the planet.
explanation.definitionFit: Whoever at all, not a particular individual, so someone with nothing special about them.

clue.text: Occupation for a man of good breeding?

definitions.text: Occupation for a man of good breeding?

parts.words: Occupation for a man of good breeding?
parts.note: good breeding suggests a well-born man, but it can also mean breeding livestock well

explanation.surface: Asking what job suits a well-bred chap.
explanation.definitionFit: A landed person of status who runs a farm, partly for pleasure, raising stock.

clue.text: Provided with means of exit, but forbidden to use it

explanation.surface: Given a way out but barred from taking it.
explanation.walkthrough: At British universities and schools, a student who is gated is confined to college as a punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Fitted with a gate, and also confined to college or home as a penalty.

clue.text: Puzzle about one sort of yellow

indicators.note: the labyrinth wraps around the numeral

parts.note: a maze is a puzzle of paths
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A puzzle concerning one shade of yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale yellow shade named after corn kernels.

clue.text: Unexpected development in dance

explanation.surface: A plot surprise turns up on the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise turn in a story, and also the 1960s dance done by swivelling the hips.

clue.text: Cynthia takes a liking to alcohol

parts.note: Cynthia is a poetic name for the moon goddess Artemis, hence the moon
to take a shine to someone is to take a liking to them

explanation.surface: A woman called Cynthia develops a fondness for drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Cynthia, a name of Artemis born on Mount Cynthus, stands for the moon in poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: Illicitly distilled spirit, especially American corn whiskey, is called this.

clue.text: Submission of note in self-justification

indicators.note: the note sits inside the word for self-justification

parts.note: a defence is an argument justifying oneself
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone submits a memo arguing their own case.
explanation.definitionFit: Respectful yielding to another's wishes or authority is a form of submission.

clue.text: Waste-disposal is hard work

indicators.note: disposal here means arrangement, as in things at one's disposal, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: Getting rid of rubbish is a laborious job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Waste-disposal' reads as one rubbish-bin term; 'disposal' is the signal to rearrange WASTE.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausting labour that makes one perspire is informally called this.
